title: Practice with the magnetic meter
html:
Learn how your iPhone responds around familiar objects before reviewing an unfamiliar space. Magnetic changes are clues—not device identities, distances, or proof of recording.

Try an unsaved practice sweep

  1. In the Guide, open Practice with the magnetometer, then choose Start Practice. Practice is also available before a magnetic Area Sweep.
  2. Compare an ordinary speaker you own with a spot away from electronics. Remove magnetic accessories if practical.
  3. Keep a gap. Move slowly over the same spot, holding the angle and distance consistent. Never press strong magnets against the phone or open equipment.
  4. Watch Actual Field and Δ Reference. Repeat the pass and learn which phone positions produce a repeatable response.

Practice does not collect Bluetooth or local-network findings, create exports, or save a session. Stop Practice, Done, or leaving the app clears the readings. Returning does not resume measurement. Begin a separate Area Sweep when ready.

Aim the sensor, not the whole phone

The sensor occupies one small point and its position varies by model. On iPhone 17 Pro Max, Apple's dimensional drawing places the compass in the lower-back area near the USB-C end—not the camera area. Do not apply this location to every iPhone.

Understand the numbers

Actual Field is measured in µT. Δ Reference is the signed difference from your display reference: a larger magnitude means a larger change, not proven proximity. Rebuild Reference changes the display comparison, not the independent event detector.

Why a visible change may not become an event

Automatic spike detection uses calibrated samples, a noise-adaptive threshold, persistence, and strong-spike rules. Small fluctuations or poor-quality measurements may not qualify. If calibration is limited, the actual-field trace can continue without automatic spike marking. Check Measurement Details; stale or unavailable readings are not a quiet field.

Completed magnetic sweeps can include Review graph, a bounded, downsampled history—not every measurement. Earlier readings may be omitted in long sweeps.

Keep the limits in view

Speakers, magnets, wiring, chargers, metal, and phone cases can all cause changes. Some cameras, microphones, and other devices produce little measurable change. A flat response does not rule out a device and is not a pass/fail test of your phone.

See the Spectra Guide for the full measurement workflow.

title: Understand Monitor and its baseline
html:
Monitor shows changes in radio observations while your iPhone stays in one place. It is not an unattended security alarm or a count of people arriving and leaving.

Establish the starting comparison

  1. Choose Monitor, select the radio measurements you need, and keep the iPhone stationary.
  2. Keep Spectra visible and the phone unlocked. Each available source needs 30 seconds of active observation; permission waiting does not count.
  3. If useful, choose Observe 30 seconds longer once to extend the comparison to 60 seconds per source.

The countdown follows the slowest participating source. No duration guarantees discovery of every device. Baseline findings remain in the final inventory: initially observed does not mean trusted.

Read changes without overinterpreting them

  • Newly observed: first observed after the starting comparison, not necessarily newly arrived.
  • Returned: an identity was observed again after a gap.
  • Not recently seen: a previously observed identity is no longer being observed. For Bluetooth, the wait is 45 seconds; local-network services follow Bonjour announcements and removals.

Sleep, identity rotation, interference, and broadcast behavior can produce these changes without physical movement. The rows count distinct identities within retained changes. One identity can appear in multiple rows, so adding them does not give a total device count.

Acknowledge or restart intentionally

Mark changes reviewed acknowledges the latest change. It does not trust a device, erase evidence, or reset the baseline. If you move or the network changes, use Monitor options → Start new baseline. Earlier comparisons remain; up to nine fit in one session.

Finish and review coverage

Choose Stop Monitor for detailed results. Switching apps or locking the iPhone ends measurement. A late or recovering source gets its own 30-second starting window rather than producing a burst of apparent arrivals. Review Coverage for source loss and interruptions.

Each comparison keeps up to 40 recent raw change events, not unlimited lifetime history. Radio intensity is not a measure of risk, and a quiet dashboard is not an all-clear.

See the Spectra Guide for complete baseline and retention details.

title: Use Spectra while traveling and in shared spaces
html:
Use Spectra to inform your next decision—not to certify that a space is safe. Silent, wired, shielded, powered-off, or unrecognizable devices can remain invisible.

Hotels, rentals, and shared housing

Start with a Quick Check to get oriented. Use an unhurried Area Sweep for accessible areas you are allowed to inspect. In gyms and changing rooms, respect other people's privacy and facility rules. A broadcast may come from outside the room; an unfamiliar name is not evidence of covert recording.

Rideshares, cafés, and travel hubs

As a passenger or while waiting, a Quick Check offers a short snapshot. Specialist checks focus on supported glasses or wearable matches. Crowds contain ordinary devices, and a name or signal strength cannot identify the person carrying one. Do not scan while driving or confront someone based on a result.

Review what the check actually covered

Inspect Coverage, clear measurement filters and name search, and consider unclassified activity. In specialist checks, View observed activity offers wider context. Expected is your label for the check, not authenticated safety. A saved check describes an earlier observation, not the space now.

Protect your connection, too

Confirm the intended Wi-Fi name with the venue through a trusted channel. A familiar network name alone does not authenticate it. Prefer cellular data when you do not trust the connection, keep software updated, protect accounts with multifactor authentication, and heed certificate warnings.

A reputable VPN can protect traffic routed through its tunnel between your phone and the VPN service; trust shifts to that provider. It does not prevent nearby recording, authenticate a hotspot, make a malicious website safe, or make you anonymous. Follow your organization's policy. VPN settings may affect local discovery; do not disable required protection or join an unfamiliar network just to find more devices. Spectra does not provide a VPN.

Keep useful context without collecting unnecessary personal details

Rename a saved session and add notes about repeatable observations, areas inspected, ordinary explanations, and unresolved questions. Notes are yours, not sensor evidence. Avoid sensitive itinerary or personal details, and review reports before sharing. Local-network browsing can send queries visible to others on that network; it is not covert.

For a credible threat or highly sensitive activity, move sensitive conversations to a more appropriate location and consult a trusted security contact. Do not tamper with equipment based on an app result.

Read the full Guide and privacy policy.

title: Contact Arc Signal support
html:
Need help with Spectra? Email support@arcsignal.zendesk.com. Please do not send passwords, account recovery codes, or payment-card details.

Include the essentials

  • What you tried, what you expected, and what happened instead.
  • The check type, selected measurements, and exact error message.
  • In iPhone Spectra Settings, use Copy support information for app, engine, catalog, hardware, and OS context. Review it before sending; it does not attach scan data.
  • For the Experimental Watch companion, include its Settings → About version, release, and build, plus whether the display dimmed or the sweep ended early.

Share only what is needed

Scan archives can include broadcast names, identifiers, network information, raw payloads, and personal notes. Start without an archive. If one is needed to investigate a problem, review the export and share it deliberately. Reduced identifying information is not anonymous. Location tags are excluded from every export unless you enable Include scan location; leave it off for support unless the location itself is necessary. This choice also applies to the reduced format. Check screenshots for personal or location details.

Nothing is sent to support automatically. Zendesk processes support information you choose to submit.

Useful links

  • Arc Signal website
  • Complete Spectra Guide
  • Spectra privacy policy

Support can help explain an app issue, but cannot certify a location as safe or provide an emergency response. For an immediate safety concern, use appropriate local assistance.
